answer: Each identity publishes a commitment to a distinct model checkpoint, and identities whose commitments or probe outputs sit too close are merged into one vote. Each epoch the network sends a fresh probe that only the committed model can answer reproducibly inside a short window. A grove of slightly tweaked copies collapses on the first hidden probe. Parking many aliases in the harbor of one base model fails: each name needs a trained delta large enough to disagree on those probes, so a farm pays for separate training runs, not just extra keys.
